questions.q: What problem does a pre-launch checklist actually solve?
options: It converts a general feeling that things are probably done into a list of specific, checkable facts
It replaces the need for any testing covered in Chapter 1
It is only useful for marketing purposes before a public launch
It guarantees a contract has zero bugs once completed
questions.explain: The risk at launch is usually something feeling done without being confirmed -- a checklist turns that feeling into specific, verifiable items.

questions.q: Why does this lesson treat 'who can touch the contract after launch' as its own checklist category, separate from the contract's correctness?
options: Because deployment and upgrade authority (multisig control, reviewed upgrade paths) matters just as much once real funds are at stake, independent of whether the code itself is correct
Because contract correctness automatically guarantees safe post-launch authority
Because this category is less important than the contract's own test suite
Because only the original deployer should ever be allowed to touch a launched contract
questions.explain: A correct contract can still be put at risk by weak post-launch authority, like a single key able to upgrade or pause it alone.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say monitoring must be live before the first real transaction, not set up afterward?
options: Configuring monitoring in a panic after something already looks wrong defeats the purpose of catching issues early
Monitoring tools cannot technically be configured before any transactions have occurred
The first transaction on a contract is never worth monitoring
Alerts calibrated after launch are always more accurate than those calibrated before
questions.explain: The entire value of monitoring and alerting is catching problems as they happen -- which requires it to already be running before real activity starts.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend actually triggering the pause mechanism before launch, rather than just confirming it exists in the code?
options: So the people who'd need to use it during a real incident have already practiced doing so, rather than using it for the first time under pressure
Triggering it before launch permanently disables the mechanism for later use
Pause mechanisms cannot be tested without affecting real user funds
It has no practical benefit over simply reading the contract's pause function
questions.explain: A rehearsed pause means the relevant people already know how to use it, rather than discovering how it works for the first time during an actual incident.

questions.q: What checklist item did this lesson deliberately leave out, reserving it for Lesson 27?
options: A security audit and bug bounty program
The smart contract's unit test suite
Hosting the frontend on a verified domain
Configuring CI to gate merges
questions.explain: Audits and bug bounties have enough depth and their own timing considerations that this lesson reserves them for Lesson 27 rather than folding them into this checklist.
